reader.requirement: The compiler must refuse a MERGE statement whose file-name-1 is not described by an SD entry visible to it, whether that name is an FD file of any organization, a GLOBAL FD of a containing program, a data-name, or no file at all, and it must accept a MERGE whose file-name-1 has an SD.
reader.edition-search: BindMerge tests file.IsSortMerge with no edition test; grep 'Edition.(Edition|DialectLevel)|DialectLevel|ConstructRegistry|Version' over StatementValidation.ResolveFile and the BindMerge region of SortBinder.cs: only the diagnostic sink (ctx.Edition / data.Edition.Error), no switch. The SD entry's closed clause list (ClosedFormatPass) also refuses GLOBAL on an SD at 85 and 2023 alike.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: l1c18-merge-file-not-sort-merge is a sequential FD only; not covered: a relative FD, a file-name that is a USING file, an undeclared name, a data-name, a containing program's SD (not visible: 1985 SD has no GLOBAL) or GLOBAL FD, and the accepting SD case at 85

reader.notes: BindMerge resolves file-name-1 through StatementValidation.ResolveFile (COBOL1639 for a name that is no file) and refuses any file whose FileModel.IsSortMerge is false (COBOL1757), at every edition by the same code. COBOL1757's text cites §2023:14.9.24.3 at --std 85 rather than §1985:XI.4.1.3 SR2, a message matter only.

refuter.evidence: Class c r6local-001 at --std 85: a containing program declares 'FD SF IS GLOBAL'; the contained program declares its own SELECT SF and 'SD SF' and runs 'MERGE SF ON ASCENDING KEY SF-KEY USING F1 F2 GIVING FO': compiled and ran, printing AAA01 / BBB02 / CCC03, so the local SD hides the global FD and file-name-1 resolves to the SD as the 1985 scope rules require (no rejection of legal source through the global name). The 1985 SD has no GLOBAL clause: the GLOBAL clause is for 'data description entries whose level-number is 01 in the File Section or the Working-Storage Section, file description entries, or report description entries' (cite.py 'OK  §1985:X.4.6.3 SR1 ... the text is in SR1'), and the Inter-Program Communication module prints GLOBAL only in the FD formats (X-15 to X-17), so the reader's refusals of a container's SD (not visible) and of 'SD SF IS GLOBAL' are right. BindMerge's IsSortMerge test has no edition switch. cite.py 'OK  §1985:XI.4.1.3 SR2  (4.1.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR2' for 'File-name-1 must be described in a sort-merge file description entry in the Data Division'.
